{{Recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the Philippines|Cuisine of the Philippines]]

'''Sopas''' is a Filipino macaroni [[Cookbook:Soup|soup]] made with elbow macaroni, meat, vegetables, and milk.

== Ingredients ==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] or [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
* 3 cloves [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* 250 grams [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] meat, still attached to the bones
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* Freshly ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]]
* 3–4 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* 1 cup dried [[Cookbook: Macaroni|elbow macaroni]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
* ½ head of [[Cookbook:Cabbage|cabbage]], shredded
* 375 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] (1½ cups) [[Cookbook:Evaporated milk|evaporated milk]]

== Procedure ==
# Preheat oil in a pot. Add onion and garlic, and sauté them. Be careful not to burn them, as this will give your soup a burnt and bitter taste.
# Add the chicken, salt, and pepper. Let it cook but don't let it brown. Browning the meat will give you a dark broth with an unpleasant taste.
# Pour in water and bring everything to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]].
# As soon as the water boils, the scum from the chicken will rise to the top—you can [[Cookbook:Skimming|skim]] it off.
# Season again with salt and pepper—this is called "layering" in cooking.
# Add the elbow macaroni and cook for 7 minutes or so.
# The macaroni will have absorbed some of the salt by now, so season again with salt.
# Add the carrots and cabbage. Mix well.
# Add in the milk but don't let it boil—boiling will make the milk separate and ruin the soup's texture.
# Serve immediately because the elbow macaroni will absorb most of the milky broth if you let it stand too long.
# Enjoy!

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Using meat with bones will make the broth tastier without the use of bouillon cubes.
* You can use [[Cookbook:Fish Sauce|fish sauce]] instead of salt for added flavor.
